A general invertible transformation, such as a permutation of the fields, is not an O(V) in-place pass; that is why interchanges are counted separately. The paper has I=3v^2 invocations (three stages, v^2 each), v=binom(h,3) (paper line 676); the factor 2 should be 3. The page also never says what an invocation or stage is.

quote: Splitting, merging and gates are a fixed number of linear passes, $O(1)$ per unit volume.
note: The recurrence F_d <= lambda F_{d-1} + O(1) also needs the cost of scheduling the s recursive calls on a fixed number of tapes (parking stack, descriptor stack) to be O(V) at each node; the paper proves this separately (lines 1560-1620). The page omits it, so the recurrence is not justified from what is given.

quote: A row addition on fields of $u=f\Omega$ bits costs $O(V(u^\tau+1))$.
note: The page never says what an address-field row addition is, why the outside work is a fixed number of them, or how its cost follows from the cited interchange cost $O(Vu^\tau)$. In the paper this comes from a fixed binary change of basis written as elementary row additions, each done by a separate lemma (paper.tex lines 2208-2232, 2290-2300).

quote: Let $\rho$ be the permutation of roles that it applies
note: The page's network consists of linear steps (with scratch roles whose values are added and restored) and it is never said why its net scalar map is a signed permutation of roles. The paper (lines 818-819) uses this only as a hypothesis ('if the scalar network is a signed role permutation'); the page asserts it as a fact about every network without stating it as a hypothesis.

quote: The leaves at depth $\nu$ have $u=f/m^\nu<d^\vartheta$ chunks
note: Here u is a number of chunks, but earlier on the same page u is a bit width (address fields of u bits, and u=f Omega bits) and no change of meaning is announced. Reading u as a bit count would make u^tau and the leaf cost inconsistent.

quote: A row addition on fields of $u=f\Omega$ bits costs $O(V(u^\tau+1))$.
note: Only the cost of an address interchange is cited; why a row addition costs O(V(u^tau+1)), and why u equals f times Omega, is not explained.

quote: the ratio is $\tfrac{3/2}{2^{0.8}}\approx1.16$
note: 2^0.8 is about 1.74, so the ratio is about 0.86, not 1.16; the stated value also contradicts the claim that lambda above 0.585 makes the ratio below 1.

quote: $N$ the number of negative source projections
note: Neither explained nor linked. In the paper (lines 1117-1118, 1162-1165) these are the source matrices -P_{U_a} assigned to the sources X_a; each makes an edge matrix of rank one where the dimension change is zero. The page also never says what dimension is meant by 'dimension changes' or 'dimension lost' (dimensions of subspaces attached to vertices).

quote: each on a stream of volume $V/W$
note: The exact volume V/W requires the stream to be split into W role streams by a row field whose length is divisible by W^k (paper lines 1481-1483, 2316-2321). The page states no row hypothesis, and gives no reason why the parameter must be a power of m, so the claim is stated without a hypothesis it needs.

quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$, so it is exact for any initial auxiliary contents.
note: The page never says how the scalar bank invocation (one scalar per triple S) becomes a shear of address fields H and D on arrays; in the paper this passes through frame identities and role streams applied to every row, including scratch roles. The identification is asserted, not derived.

quote: so $2L>N$ and $s<WD$
note: Inequality reversed. L/N=100/539 gives 2L/N=200/539<1, so 2L<N, not 2L>N. s=WD-N+2L<WD holds exactly because 2L<N; 2L>N would give s>WD. The paper has L<N/2 (line 895) and deficit N-2L>0 (line 1167).

quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
note: The leaf 'kernel' is never defined or linked, so the reader does not know what it does or why it costs O(f/m^nu) per unit volume.

quote: The network's rank budget, which counts dimension changes along its edges, gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
note: The identity is asserted with no derivation or statement of what the rank budget is; the reader cannot check it from the page.

quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
note: The citation stands in for the page's own concept and the page does not say what is meant by 'keeps' or why it applies to auxiliary roles. It is also in tension with the claim that auxiliary values are restored, since the endpoint operator D_sink D_source^{-1} is not shown to be the identity for them.

quote: So the shear needs $2\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
note: Inconsistent with the page. Each update takes one interchange and there are rank_Q M ones in Pi, so the count is rank_Q M, not twice that. The later definition of s_b as the sum of the ranks also counts one per rank.

quote: $N$ the number of negative source projections
note: The page neither explains nor links 'negative source projections', and a reader with this background does not know the term.

quote: Both are $O(m^{k\tau})$, since $m\ge2$.
note: The page only says to fix tau<1, but the bound k = O(m^{k tau}) for the case s/W <= 1 needs tau>0, and m>=2 alone does not give it. The paper chooses tau in (0,1) (line 1478, and 0<tau<1 at line 1343). The hypothesis m>=2 is also never stated earlier on the page (paper line 1450).

quote: Signed label changes telescope along each wire, and gate labels cancel.
note: The page does not say why gate labels cancel, why the sinks receiving the sources have label U_iota-perp, or why the remaining sinks have full label F, so the signed total WD-2N cannot be checked.

quote: The first edge out of each source has matrix $2P_{U_\iota}$, rank one, with no label change
note: The matrix 2P is stated without derivation, though sources were given -P.

quote: The paper's decisive property is a bound on the number of smaller calls, (cited).
note: The page does not say what the bound is or how s<WD yields it, so the role of the cited result is unclear.

quote: If $\lambda\le1$ the sum is at most $d$.
note: The sum 1+lambda+...+lambda^d has d+1 terms each at most 1, so it is at most d+1, not d. The O() conclusion still holds.

quote: a forward invocation from $X$ to $Y$ subtracts $x_S$ from $y_S$
note: The paper's Lemma scalar-motifs (line 729-731) says a forward invocation changes y_S to y_S + x_S, i.e. it adds x_S to y_S. The page itself then identifies it with the shear H <- H+D, which adds, so 'subtracts' is inconsistent with the page and wrong. Also the paper's forward, inverse, forward schedule sends (X,Y) to (-Y,X), an exchange only in the bit construction.

quote: A row addition on fields of $u=f\Omega$ bits costs $O(V(u^\tau+1))$.
note: The page cites only the interchange cost and never explains why a row addition costs this or why the outside work is a fixed number of row additions.

quote: Sources have dimension $1$, summing to $N$; sinks have dimension $D$, except the $N$ sinks that receive the sources
note: The page never states the prescribed source and sink labels: X-sources U_iota, all other sources 0, X and scratch sinks F, Y sinks U_iota^perp. 'Sources have dimension 1' is true only for the N X-sources. The telescoping claim 'gate labels cancel' also rests on gate labels that are never given (paper lines 881-889, 975-988).

quote: A row addition on fields of $u=f\Omega$ bits costs $O(V(u^\tau+1))$.
note: The page cites only the interchange cost O(Vu^tau) and never says how a row addition is built from or bounded by interchanges. In the paper this is Lemma packed-selected-bit-rectangle (line 2298), not stated here.

quote: The paper's decisive property is a bound on the number of smaller calls, (cited).
note: The cited bound is not stated, nor how s<WD yields it.

quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
note: Does not follow from the preceding sentences, which only require q not to divide denominators so that mu*xi^{-1} makes sense mod q^b. The paper (lines 1415-1421) chooses q to avoid every denominator in the finite table and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor, so the triangular factors stay invertible mod q^b. The page does not say why numerators matter, and it states the condition for all numerators, which is wider than the paper requires.

quote: which is $O(f^\lambda)$ when $\lambda>\tau(1+\eta/\vartheta)$
note: The page later takes lambda with log_m(s/W)<lambda<1 and uses the same lambda for the outside-work bound. Such a lambda exists only if tau(1+eta/vartheta)<1, i.e. tau(1+2 eta)<1. The page states only tau<1 and eta>0, so this hypothesis is missing.

quote: Since $\mu<2^{20}$
note: The page never gives mu for the explicit network (nor W_b, s_b), and does not cite this bound, so the reader cannot check that mu < 2^20.

quote: fix $\tau<1$ with $s/W>m^\tau$
note: Wrong direction and inconsistent with the page's own later use ('because $s/W<m^\tau$') and with the geometric-sum argument. The paper (Proposition power-interchange, paper.tex line 1480) chooses a rational tau in (0,1) with s/W < m^tau; since s/W < m and m^tau -> m, such tau exists. With s/W > m^tau the recurrence would give a worse exponent.

quote: So the signed total is $WD-2N$.
note: The page does not say how many sinks there are (W of them), which sinks receive the sources, or why the signed total is sinks minus sources.

quote: Undoing the exchange moves each output back to its input role, and multiplying by $-\varepsilon_w$ again removes the sign.
note: The page never says what 'undoing the exchange' is (a second pass, an inverse network?) nor how it combines with the route operator, so the reader cannot check that it restores values.

quote: nondegenerate subspace
note: Nondegenerate for the indefinite form I-J/9 is never defined or linked; needed for projection along U^perp.

quote: The leaves at depth $\nu$ have $u=f/m^\nu<d^\vartheta$ chunks
note: Earlier on the page u is a field width in bits (u=f*Omega bits). Here u counts chunks, a different quantity, so the reader cannot tell which meaning u carries in the leaf cost O((s/W)^nu u).

quote: Per wire, the interchanges are fewer than $R$
note: s_b < W_b R only gives fewer than R interchanges per wire on average, not on every wire. The statement is stronger than what supports it.

quote: $N$ the number of negative source projections
note: The terms 'negative source projection', 'decreasing edge', 'dimension lost' and 'rank budget' are not explained, and the bit network and its matrices on edges are not described. The reader cannot interpret N and L_b or check the formula for s_b.

quote: For a scratch role the construction has $\rho(w)=w$ with sign $+1$ (cited)
note: The construction is never given, so the reader cannot check that scratch roles are fixed with sign +1. The cited claim carries the page's own concept.

quote: its operator is $D_\nu$, however many gates it passes through
note: The page just said the route applies epsilon_w D_sink D_source^{-1}; with source frame I and sink frame D_nu the operator is epsilon_w D_nu, and equals D_nu only when the sign is +1. The example omits the sign, inconsistent with the earlier statement (paper line 821: epsilon_w D_sink D_source^{-1}).

quote: A level-$k$ call makes $s$ calls at level $k-1$
note: The page never says how a level-k interchange of fields of m^k bits gives s interchanges of m^(k-1)-bit fields. It does not say that H and D are cut into m sub-fields, that each edge of the network applies a shear given by an m by m rational matrix, or that an edge of rank a costs exactly a half-width interchanges. 'Rank reduced by a lower-triangular factorization' gives no argument for this, so the reader cannot check the recurrence.

quote: For any initial auxiliary values
note: Auxiliary values and auxiliary wires are not explained or linked. The reader knows wires, banks and forward invocation, but not which wires are auxiliary.

quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
note: The page only requires that q not divide the denominators xi. It does not follow that q divides no numerator (zero entries have numerator 0), and the needed claim that the factor matrices F_1, F_2 and their inverses are invertible mod q is never justified.

quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
note: The kernel, the leaf and the per-chunk handling are never defined, and why the cost is O(f/m^nu) is not given.

quote: So the shear needs $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
note: The O(V) bound is cited only for lower-triangular transformations of one vector. The two additions D_tau += H_sigma and D_tau = H_sigma - D_tau act on pairs of fields across the two vectors, and the page never says they are linear-cost or lower-triangular (e.g. in the stacked order (H,D)), nor how the interchanges and additions are costed on tapes.

quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$, so it is exact for any initial auxiliary contents.
note: Inconsistent with the paper and with the page's own description. In the paper X and Y are banks of bit values on wires, and the forward invocation adds x_S to y_S pointwise over F_2 (Lemma scalar-motifs, lines 729-731). The address shear H<-H+D over Z/qZ is not that invocation: it is produced by applying the frame permutations Phi_{A_e} to each role stream and the endpoint identity M_out(rho(w)) - M_in(w) = I (lines 1534-1545), with scratch roles handled because their initial values are arbitrary. D and H are address fields, not the banks X and Y. The page's identification is wrong and gives no argument.

quote: $N$ the number of negative source projections
note: Neither 'negative source projection', 'decreasing edges', 'dimension lost' nor the 'rank budget' of the bit network is defined or linked. The reader knows only generic linear networks with roles and frames.

quote: The first edge out of each source has matrix $2P_{U_\iota}$, rank one, with no label change
note: This needs the source matrix -P_{U_iota} (so only the X sources, not each source) and that the first gate has label exactly U_iota, so the edge difference is P_U-(-P_U)=2P_U; the page states neither the gate label nor that an edge matrix is head minus tail. In the paper this holds at stage 1 where B=0 (lines 1163-1164).

quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
note: This does not follow from the preceding sentences, which only require q not to divide the denominators xi. The needed hypothesis is also different: the paper (Lemma matrix-shear proof, lines 1415-1418) takes q avoiding every denominator in the finite table of factors and inverses and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor, so that the triangular factors stay invertible mod q^b (the page never says why F_1, F_2 stay invertible modulo q^b, nor that such a q exists). Avoiding all numerators and denominators is only a sufficient example in the paper.

quote: Elimination shows this: pivot on the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clear its left and lower entries by lower-triangular operations, and repeat on what remains.
note: Only a terse sketch: it does not say which clearing is a row or column operation, why both sides stay lower triangular, or why the result is a partial permutation with exactly rank M ones; the reader cannot check the claim.

quote: So the signed total is $WD-2N$.
note: The count of sinks is never given, so the reader cannot see why there are W of dimension D. Nor can they see how the source, sink and telescoping terms combine into WD-2N, or why the extra N is then added back.

quote: Both are $O(m^{k\tau})$, since $m\ge2$.
note: Bounding k (the s/W<=1 case) by O(m^{k tau}) needs tau>0, which the page never states (it only says tau<1), and m>=2 is not given where m is introduced. The hypothesis 0<tau<1 and m>=2 should be stated.

quote: Each edge of the bit network carries such a matrix.
note: The page never says what matrix an edge carries. In the paper (lines 1146-1150, 1461) it is the difference M_head - M_tail of the matrices assigned to the edge's two end vertices, not a matrix attached to the edge itself. The page does not describe the vertex matrices or the network's labels, so the reader cannot check that the ranks of these differences sum to s_b.

quote: and the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$.
note: The inequality does not follow from f>=d^vartheta, the only relation between f and d. It needs d^(vartheta(1-sigma)) <= f^(lambda-sigma), i.e. f >= d^(vartheta(1-sigma)/(lambda-sigma)), which is a stronger condition because (1-sigma)/(lambda-sigma)>1. Otherwise the bound carries a factor depending on d, and f^sigma d^(vartheta(1-sigma)) can be as large as f. The hypothesis is missing.

quote: A field of $u=m^k$ bits therefore has $Q_k=O(u^\tau)$
note: The recurrence proves the bound only for widths that are powers of m, and only when a row field preceding both chunks has length divisible by W^k (paper Proposition power-interchange, lines 1475-1487). The page states no such row hypothesis. The step from this case to arbitrary field widths u, as in the page's opening claim and the O(Vu^tau) bound, is Lemma chunk-swap (lines 1631-1660), which the page does not mention.

quote: Taking $\lambda$ with $\log_m(s/W)<\lambda<1$ makes the ratio below 1
note: The choice of lambda also has to satisfy lambda > tau(1+eta/vartheta) from the outside-work bound, and lambda > tau, sigma. That is possible only if eta is small enough that tau(1+eta/vartheta)<1; the page says only that eta>0 is fixed. The paper (lines 2394-2399) requires max{tau,sigma}<lambda<1 and tau(1+c/beta)<lambda, so the page is missing the hypothesis on eta and the full list of conditions on lambda.

quote: the $s$ smaller calls are interchanges of width $\mu^{d-1}$
note: The page never says that each width-mu^d chunk is cut into mu fields of width mu^{d-1}, that H and D are then vectors of mu fields, or that the shear H+MD for a mu x mu matrix M of rank a is done by exactly a interchanges of such fields (paper Lemma matrix-shear, line 1394, and line 1495). This link between the mu x mu vertex matrices and the width mu^d is why a rank-a edge costs a calls of width mu^{d-1}, and the page only asserts it.

quote: For a scratch role the construction has $\rho(w)=w$ with sign $+1$ (cited)
note: The page never states the wiring, so the reader cannot check that scratch roles return to themselves with sign +1; this stands in for how the network works.

quote: distinct triples are orthogonal
note: The form gives |T cap S|-1, which is zero only when |T cap S|=1; for disjoint triples it is -1 and for overlap 2 it is 1, so orthogonality of all distinct triples does not follow from what is shown.

quote: the number of negative source projections
note: Negative source projections and decreasing edges are never defined, so the reader cannot tell what N and L_b measure or why N > 2 L_b is plausible.

quote: At depth $d$, the $s$ smaller calls are interchanges of width $\mu^{d-1}$ on streams of volume $V/W$
note: The paper's Proposition (line 1475-1490) needs fields over a fixed prime radix q, widths that are powers m^k of m measured in radix-q digits, and a row field before both chunks of length divisible by W^k so that the row split into W streams can be repeated d times. The page omits all of these, mixes width in bits (u) with width in digits (mu^d), and never explains how arbitrary u is reached from powers of mu (paper Lemma, lines 1631-1740: padding rows and base-m decomposition), so the claimed O(V u^tau) for arbitrary u does not follow from the recursion shown.

quote: The paper shows $N<2L_{\rm b}$, so $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}R$.
note: The inequality is reversed and the conclusion does not follow. With s_b = W_b R - N + 2L_b, s_b < W_b R holds exactly when N > 2L_b; N < 2L_b would give s_b > W_b R. The paper (lines 1107-1109, L_b/N = 100/539 < 1/2; line 1167, 'Its deficit from W_b m is N-2L_b>0') shows N > 2L_b. Correct statement: the paper shows N>2L_b, so s_b<W_b R.

quote: the number of central wires in one invocation
note: The page never says which wires of the network are central, nor how an invocation has a number of them; the linear network concept only covers wires, banks and forward invocation.

quote: Since $\mu<2^{20}$
note: The page never gives the value of mu for the explicit network; the bound mu<2^20 comes from m=h^3=10^6 in the paper (line 1332 uses m<2^20, definition at line 654). The reader cannot check it.

quote: The paper cites this factorization from earlier work without proof; elimination proves it
note: Inconsistent with the paper: Lemma lower-lower (paper.tex lines 1364-1392) gives the elementary elimination proof itself, citing Grigor'ev only for the name (Bruhat factorization with reversed coordinate order, lines 1358-1362). The paper does not cite it without proof.

quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$
note: A forward invocation subtracts x_S from y_S, so with D as X and H as Y it computes H <- H - D. The page defines the shear as H <- H + D. The sign is inconsistent; either the shear is H - D or the invocation adds, and the page does not reconcile them.

quote: and the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$
note: The last inequality is not justified and is false in general. At a call that has internal levels, f >= d^vartheta, so f^sigma d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} only gives about f, not f^lambda with lambda<1. The paper (lines 2430-2435) stops at O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and absorbs it only in the final bound O(d^{lambda'}) with lambda' > max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)} (lines 2455-2460), using e <= d.

quote: Signed label changes telescope along each wire, and gate labels cancel.
note: The page never says how each edge's matrix or signed change is defined or which labels the edges join, so the telescoping and cancellation cannot be checked.

quote: multiplying by $-\varepsilon_w$ again removes the sign
note: Wrong sign. The route multiplies the array by eps_w in {+1,-1}; to remove it one multiplies by eps_w again (eps_w^2=1), not by -eps_w, which would leave a factor -1 on every role with eps_w=+1. It also contradicts the next claim that scratch roles (sign +1) need no correction. The paper (lines 1312-1313) only negates the outputs that carry the minus sign, i.e. multiplies by eps_w.

quote: which the recurrence turns into a saving of a power of the chunk width
note: The page refers to 'the recurrence' without stating it. The paper (lines 1536-1560, equation swap-recurrence) uses F_0=O(1), F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), whose geometric sum gives time O(V e^tau) for chunk length e=m^k when s/W < m^tau. The reader cannot see how 'fewer than R interchanges per wire' yields a power saving.

quote: its operator is $D_\nu$, however many gates it passes through.
note: The page just said the route applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}. With source frame I and sink frame D_nu the operator is eps_w D_nu, equal to D_nu only when the sign is +1 (as for scratch roles). The paper (line 144-146) gives the scalar sign together with the endpoint operator.

quote: Each of the $2\binom h3^2$ invocations has $h$ central wires
note: The page never says what an invocation is or why there are that many, and never explains which edges decrease or why each loses h, when the only label growth stated is h-2 dimensions.

quote: The paper's decisive property is a bound on the number of smaller calls, (cited).
note: The bound is never stated and the sentence is incomplete. The reader is not told what s < WD yields for the number of smaller calls, or why it gives the power saving.

quote: which the recurrence turns into a saving of a power of the chunk width (the chunk length)
note: The page has not introduced any recurrence or chunking, and gives no link to where they are defined. The reader cannot check how fewer than R interchanges per wire becomes a power saving.

quote: Sources have dimension $1$, summing to $N$; sinks have dimension $D$, except the $N$ sinks that receive the sources
note: The page never gives the terminal labels. Only the N sources of the first bank have the line label U_iota (dimension 1); the other bank's and scratch sources have label 0, so 'Sources have dimension 1' is overstated. Likewise the sinks with label U_iota^perp (dimension D-1) are those of the second bank (paper lines 881-892). The claim that central wires are the only decreasing edges, each losing exactly h, is also asserted without the gate schedule or labels (paper Lemma on residuals, lines 1000-1070), so the reader cannot check L.

quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
note: The page does not say what 'keeps' means or how restoring auxiliary values follows from the telescoping, and the claim is only cited.

quote: Over $\mathbb F_2$ each update is a pointwise XOR, since addition and subtraction are the same operation
note: The three updates D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D are carried out over Z/q^b Z with q an odd prime (paper lines 1415-1417, 1535-1540), so they are not XORs and after the first update D holds D-H mod q^b, not the XOR of D and H. Only the circuit's gates are pointwise XOR gates (paper line 1139); the address updates are not, so the page conflates the two.

quote: A label $U$ is a nondegenerate subspace of $\mathcal F$.
note: Nondegenerate with respect to a bilinear form (needed so that F = U + U-perp and P_U exists) is not explained; the form I-J/9 is indefinite, so orthogonal complements need not be complementary, and an undergraduate reader knows only dot products.

quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
note: The page does not say what 'keeps' means or why undoing the exchange leaves the endpoint operator. It also appears to conflict with the opening claim that every auxiliary value is restored: a scratch route applies D_sink D_source^{-1}, which is the identity only if the two frames agree, and the page never states this hypothesis.

quote: and the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$.
note: The last inequality is not justified. The page only gives $f\ge d^\vartheta$ at internal nodes, which yields $d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)}\le f^{1-\sigma}$ and so only $O(f)$. To reach $O(f^\lambda)$ one needs $d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)}\le f^{\lambda-\sigma}$, i.e. $f\ge d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)/(\lambda-\sigma)}$, or $d$ treated as a constant factor; neither is stated.

quote: Per wire, the interchanges are fewer than $R$
note: What is shown is s_b < W_b R, a bound on the total over all wires. It gives fewer than R interchanges per wire only on average, not for each wire. The correct statement is that the interchanges number fewer than R per wire on average.

quote: The outside work is a fixed number of address-field row additions.
note: The page never says what a row of an address field is, why a call's own work consists of a fixed number of row additions, or why the cited interchange bound O(Vu^tau) gives the row-addition cost O(V(u^tau+1)) (the paper, around lines 2226-2300, uses a separate packed-selected-bit-rectangle lemma and a fixed binary change of basis for this). The reader cannot check this from the page.

quote: Since $\mu<2^{20}$
note: The bound mu < 2^20 for the explicit network is neither derived nor cited, yet the choice of tau and the final inequality depend on it.

quote: Every fixed-tape procedure of the argument comes from one and the same network
note: Contradicts the paper, which says each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network (paper.tex line 116: 'Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values'). The page itself later treats different networks and frames (a route from a source frame I to a sink frame D). Correct: every procedure comes from a network of this kind, not a single shared network.

quote: and the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$
note: The first bound is correct: (s/W)^nu u <= (f/u)^sigma u = f^sigma u^(1-sigma) < f^sigma d^(vartheta(1-sigma)). The second inequality is not justified. The page itself uses only d <= f^(1/vartheta), which gives d^(vartheta(1-sigma)) <= f^(1-sigma) and so only O(f), not O(f^lambda). The step holds only if d is treated as a constant, which contradicts the earlier substitution d <= f^(1/vartheta). Correct statement: the leaf cost is O(f^sigma d^(vartheta(1-sigma))), which is O(f^lambda) only under an extra assumption such as d^vartheta <= f^((lambda-sigma)/(1-sigma)) or d bounded.

quote: which is $O(f^\lambda)$ when $\lambda>\tau(1+\eta/\vartheta)$
note: Missing hypothesis: the page also needs lambda<1, so it needs tau(1+eta/vartheta)<1, which does not follow from tau<1 and eta>0 alone; eta must be small enough. Without this the range for lambda may be empty.

quote: Both are $O(m^{k\tau})$, since $m\ge2$.
note: The page never states m>=2 (the paper fixes integers m,W>=2 at line 1463), and it does not say how m>=2 gives either bound. It is only needed for k+1=O(m^{k tau}) in the case s/W<=1, which the page does not treat.

quote: Since $\mu<2^{20}$

A hypothesis is missing (pivots must be q-adic units, or the factors shown q-integral). Also, the pivot should be the rightmost nonzero entry of the row, not just the rightmost entry.

quote: Let $s$, the total rank over all edges, change meaning here. Each unit of rank costs one smaller call. (cited)
note: The page never says which matrix has a rank on an edge (the difference of head and tail matrices, which is what P_V - P_U is), and never says what a smaller call is or why one unit of rank costs one. The cited claim stands in for the mechanism linking the network to the recursion.

quote: Each role stream then holds $V/(2W)$ bits (cited).
note: Cyclic distribution of rows over W roles suggests V/W bits per role; the factor 2 is not explained and the page never says why it applies. The cited claim stands in for the page's own count.

quote: the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$
note: f >= d^vartheta only gives d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} <= f^{1-sigma}, hence a bound O(f), not O(f^lambda). The inequality needs a stronger hypothesis such as f >= d^{vartheta(1-sigma)/(lambda-sigma)}, or d treated as a constant; the page does not state it.

quote: Both are $O(m^{k\tau})$, since $m\ge2$.
note: Missing hypothesis. Bounding k (case s/W<=1) by O(m^{k tau}) needs m^tau>1, i.e. tau>0, but the page only says 'fix tau<1'. The paper chooses tau in (0,1) (Proposition power-interchange, line 1481; also line 1555-1556). m>=2 alone does not suffice.

quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk
note: The reader is never told what a kernel is or why a leaf costs O(f/m^nu).

quote: and it has $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ ones
note: Stated about every partial permutation matrix, which is false: a partial permutation matrix can have any number of ones. Only the Pi produced by the factorization of M has exactly rank M ones (paper line 1370-1372, Pi has exactly a entries equal to one). Also the page does not argue why elimination ends with exactly rank-many ones.

quote: by a restoration device the paper introduces as new
note: Misattribution. The paper (lines 708-711) says the cancellation of arbitrary initial scratch values is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation of Buhrman, Cleve, Koucky, Loff and Speelman, not a device it introduces. Also the paper's lemma (line 729-737) gives (X,Y) -> (-Y,X), which is an exchange only in the bit (F_2) construction.

quote: so the internal sum is at most a constant times $f^\lambda$ for every $\lambda>0$
note: Stated too widely. The geometric series converges only when the ratio is below 1, i.e. $\lambda>\log_m(s/W)$, and the outside-work bound also needs $\lambda>\tau(1+\eta/\vartheta)$. The paper takes $\max\{\tau,\sigma\}<\lambda<1$ with $\tau(1+c/\beta)<\lambda$ (paper.tex lines 2400-2420), not every $\lambda>0$.

quote: The coefficients come from the finitely many matrices, not from $V$, and $R$ is fixed, so each pass is linear.
note: The fields act by mu * xi^{-1} modulo q^b, and xi^{-1} mod q^b is a b-digit number that depends on b, hence on V, so it is not a fixed coefficient. Linear time needs the argument that multiplying by the integer mu and dividing exactly by xi (digit by digit mod q^b) are linear passes; the page does not say this.

quote: Let $F_d$ be the time per unit volume of a width-$\mu^d$ interchange
note: The page never says how a mu x mu vertex matrix relates to width mu^d: each chunk is split into mu consecutive fields of width mu^(d-1), the matrix acts on these mu fields, and the pivot pairs of those fields are the smaller interchanges (paper lines 1498-1500, 1527-1531). Without this the claim that the smaller calls have width mu^(d-1) cannot be checked.

quote: For a scratch role the construction has $\rho(w)=w$ with sign $+1$ (cited), so the undoing needs no correction there.
note: 'The construction' of the network is never described, so the cited fact that scratch roles have rho(w)=w and sign +1 stands in for how the concept works. Even so, such a route applies D_sink(w) D_source(w)^{-1}, which is not the identity unless the two frames agree, so 'needs no correction' is not justified.

quote: have $u=f/m^\nu<d^\vartheta$ chunks
note: u was just defined as a bit width, u = f*Omega bits, and is now a number of chunks, u = f/m^nu, without any notice that the letter changes meaning (the page flags other such changes). The two uses are inconsistent.

quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
note: Only q not dividing the denominators was required; a numerator can be 0 or a multiple of q, so the 'So' does not follow, and the reader cannot see why the matrices stay invertible mod q.

quote: A label $U$ is a nondegenerate subspace of $\mathcal F$.
note: Nondegenerate subspace of a space with a bilinear form is not defined or linked, and is beyond dot products and orthogonality as taught. The page also gives a form only on Q^h and never says F carries the tensor-product form or that it is nondegenerate, yet needs it for U^perp, P_U and the decomposition U plus U^perp.

quote: which gives $s<Wm$ smaller calls
note: The linked page proves s<Wm with m the dimension of the fixed space; here m is the factor by which the parameter grows. The page never says these coincide, so the claim cannot be checked.
